abstract: Intratubular seminomas of the testis associated with solid tumors were studied by light and electron microscopy in order to obtain information about the earliest stage of emigration from the tubules and invasion of the interstitial space. Careful examination of numerous sections reveals that at this stage neoplastic cells protrude into evaginations of the tubule covered by basement membrance or directly invade that membrane. At the site of tumor cell emigration, the basement membrane is thickened and multilayered. Tumor cells devoid of basement membrane were found in the interstitium. Their transmigration through the basement membrane was never observed. Subsequent to the migration of seminoma cells the tubules are smaller in diameter and contain only Sertoli cells. From the observations described it is inferred that tumor cells in the interstitial tissue increase in number, form strands and lobules, and finally build up the solid tumor.
abstract_ja: 精細管内セミノーマを伴う精巣の充実性腫瘍について、光学顕微鏡および電子顕微鏡で検討し、腫瘍細胞が精細管から間質へ遊走する最初期段階の情報を得た。多数の切片を注意深く観察したところ、この段階で腫瘍細胞は基底膜で覆われた精細管の陥入部へ突出するか、その膜を直接浸潤していた。腫瘍細胞が遊走する部位では基底膜が肥厚して多層化していた。基底膜を欠く腫瘍細胞が間質に認められたが、基底膜の通過は一度も観察されなかった。セミノーマ細胞が遊走した後、精細管は直径が小さくなり、セルトリ細胞のみを含むようになる。以上の観察から、間質の腫瘍細胞は数を増やして索状および小葉状を形成し、最終的に充実性腫瘍を構築すると推測される。
